scope: Player pack v21: what differs from v20, how the six moved Pixelmon default keys were checked, and what was not checked. No game client was started.
requested_by: The owner asked for a new pack after the final review reported that six Pixelmon keys act together with Society-side keys

built_from.server_profile: Staged from merge commit 0453486f046bd3078199140155e10a400631496f with tools/stage_forge_candidate.py --mode player; byte-identical to the profile that passed the full game check in final-review-2026-11-14.json

v20_to_v21.default_key_file_change: Six lines added after the last key line; no other line changed

moved_keys.action: Fold or unfold the Pokemon overlay
moved_keys.note: No other default binding. Three situations read the 0 key directly: the F3 profiler chart while it is shown, Supplementaries while a quiver-type item is in use, and the port's Linked Typewriter while a player operates one.
Scholar reads its key only inside its book editing screen and Pixelmon acts only while no screen is open, so no press runs both. The two still show as a conflict in the controls screen.

moved_keys.action: Open the wiki page of the block in view

left_as_they_are.also_acts: Shoulder Surfing camera distance, only in the shoulder view
Tool Belt menu, only while a belt is worn

verification.reviewers: Two independent Claude Opus agents, each given the built pack and no conclusion to confirm; the facts they reported about Scholar, Sophisticated Core, More Minecarts, Better Advanced Tooltips, libtooltips, Decorative Blocks and Kiwi were then re-read from the disassembled classes before entering the table

free_key_scan.method: Superclass of all 79,143 classes of the 355 mod JARs and 184 nested JARs read to find every KeyMapping type (38); every construction site of those types resolved to name and coded key (194 sites, plus enum and wrapper registrations traced by hand); every method in all JARs searched for the six key codes and the key-handling ones (50) read one by one; vanilla KeyboardHandler, Minecraft, Gui, KeyboardInput and Options disassembled
free_key_scan.of_those: 19 Pixelmon, 3 of the port, 17 of Society's own mods (Scholar 7, More Minecarts 2, libtooltips 1, Better Advanced Tooltips 2, Decorative Blocks 1, Oculus 1, Kiwi 1, Sophisticated Core 2); all are in the key table

per_key.semicolon: No other default binding, no direct use with no screen open
per_key.apostrophe: No other default binding, no direct use with no screen open
per_key.f8: No other default binding, no direct use with no screen open
per_key.home: No other default binding; the only direct uses are cursor movement inside text fields of screens
per_key.0: No other default binding. Direct uses with no screen open, each in a mode the player turns on: vanilla F3 profiler chart selection, Supplementaries slot selection while a quiver-type item is in use, the port's Linked Typewriter while a player operates one
per_key.f6: Scholar's key.scholar.import_book has F6 as its coded default (universal context, no modifier) and no line in the default key file. Scholar reads it only in its book editing screen; Pixelmon's quest journal acts through consumeClick, which is fed only while no screen is open. No single press runs both. Forge's conflict rule marks the two as conflicting in the controls screen (read from the code, not run)

free_key_scan.first_build_finding: The first table listed only the Pixelmon and port bindings as coded defaults, so the tool did not see Scholar's F6. The table now lists all 39 and is pinned to the mod lock; the tool accepts a target key only when the bindings on it are exactly the ones the table declares

configured_defaults_merge.method: The real fuzs.configureddefaults.handler.CopyDefaultsHandler.initialize(gameDir, true) from the pack's ConfiguredDefaults-v8.0.4 JAR, one JVM per case

cases.result: options.txt equals the v21 default key file; the six lines are present

cases.case: v20 instance whose options.txt the game has saved (Pixelmon keys written at their old keys)
cases.result: File not rewritten; the six new defaults have no effect

cases.case: v20 instance whose options.txt the game never saved
cases.result: File rewritten with exactly the six lines appended
No Pixelmon key line; the coded defaults G, B, O, N, M, K apply

configured_defaults_merge.when_the_game_first_saves: Read from the client classes: among others on first opening Multiplayer (the warning screen) and on the first server join. A player who has joined the server therefore has a saved file

forge_side.method: Disassembly of Options, ClientModLoader, ForgeHooksClient and Minecraft from the Forge 47.4.20 client JAR; the real InputConstants and KeyModifier classes run standalone
findings: Key lines of mod bindings are read by Options.load(true) from ClientModLoader.finishModLoading, after RegisterKeyMappingsEvent
A value such as key.keyboard.home:NONE is split at the colon and parsed with KeyModifier.valueFromString and InputConstants.getKey; the game itself writes no :NONE suffix and reads both forms
The six names resolve to key codes 59, 39, 48, 295, 297, 268
An unknown key name would throw and stop the rest of the options from loading; the tool only accepts names from the game's own list
All six actions run from the binding itself (consumeClick); no hard-coded key code for them. DebugKeyBindings compares O and K only while F3 is held, for its debug toggles
Key hints Pixelmon draws use the bound key's display name; no hint text in en_us or ko_kr names one of the six letters

not_verified: No client was started with v21: the import, the six keys in play, the controls screen and the display names of ; and ' on other keyboard layouts are unconfirmed
Whether both listeners really act on the old shared keys was traced in bytecode during the final review and never pressed in game
Key handling that never uses the key code as a constant (read from a config file at run time), scancode-based handling and controller mappings are outside the scan

The unmoved Pixelmon keys C, H, P, U, V, Y share a plain key with Society bindings that the final review judged gated or inert, and S, R, W of the PC screen are read only inside that screen; none of this was looked at again here
